purpose: Maps governed technical DQ conditions to non-financial, non-causal impact hypotheses. These mappings do not assert customer harm, regulatory breach, financial loss, or operational loss.

data_integrity.description: Reliability of structured data used for analytics, reporting, and monitoring.

interaction_analytics_reliability.description: Reliability of transcript-derived interaction analysis and trend interpretation.

privacy_and_data_handling.description: Need for controlled review of possible sensitive-data exposure in structured transcript fields.

operational_monitoring.description: Ability to monitor and compare operational patterns across periods or approved dimensions.

model_and_rule_input_quality.description: Suitability of structured transcript fields for downstream rules, models, and decision support.

conditions.hypothesis_template: Observed speaker-attribution quality issues may reduce confidence in analysis that depends on distinguishing conversation participants.
Observed topic-distribution change may affect comparability of interaction trends across evaluated periods or approved segments.
Observed transcript-duration plausibility exceptions may reduce confidence in downstream analysis that relies on transcript size or interaction-duration relationships.
Observed structured-data completeness gaps may limit the coverage and comparability of analytics, monitoring, or downstream rule inputs.
Observed suspected mistranscription patterns may reduce the reliability of transcript-derived categorization and analysis.
Observed privacy-pattern detections require controlled technical and policy review; the detection alone does not establish a breach or exposure event.
Observed token-quality exceptions may reduce confidence in transcript-derived keywords, classification, and analysis when governed vocabulary coverage is sufficient.
